## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

Check the target project for existing components, layout patterns,and tokens that match the design intent. Reuse what the project already has instead of generating new code from sc… [truncated]

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence ("in 2 weeks", "every Monday") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.

- validate-only: Market and business model validation for a Scout-approved idea. Takes ~1 week.
- shape-only: 2-day kill test for a raw SaaS idea. Fast validation before investing time.
- saas-cycle: Full SaaS idea-to-verdict pipeline. Takes an idea from raw concept through build, launch, and mea...

Auto-triggers when staging changes.

**Gap 2: Ecom motion + interaction specialist.** Elio is "Ecom UI specialist" (storefront/PDP/cart/checkout) but ecom CRO winners differentiate on micro-interactions (image zoom, variant swatches, sticky ATC, cart drawer, swipe gestures, exit-intent). 2. **Roster gap.** Quill = SaaS marketing. Spark = hero/CTA above-fold. Sequence = lifecycle email. Hydrogen architecture (RSC + Oxygen). React Router 7 file conventions. Cart API patterns. Customer Account API. Storefront API GraphQL queries. Image optimization (Shopify CDN). ### `standalone-stack-c.md`
Custom React Router 7 + Tailwind/shadcn ecom storefront (no Hydrogen). Headless commerce APIs (Shopify Storefront API, BigCommerce, Medusa). State management (cart in cookie + server actions). ### `standalone-stack-c.md`
Custom React Router 7 + Tailwind/shadcn ecom storefront (no Hydrogen). Headless commerce APIs (Shopify Storefront API, BigCommerce, Medusa). State management (cart in cookie + server actions). Auth patterns (passwordless, social, account). Payment integration (Shop Pay, Stripe, PayPal). SEO (server-rendered, structured data). Performance (LCP <2.0s ecom standard).

### `polaris-vs-storefront-tokens.md`
Critical: Polaris is for ADMIN ONLY. Storefront tokens come from project design system or theme. Token bridge mapping (Polaris → Tailwind). Color/spacing/type scale conversion table. When to use shadcn vs custom for ecom storefront. Dark mode handling for storefront (often opt-in, not system-driven). Brand customization layer.

---

## Stack Decision Matrix

| Use case | Stack | Notes |
|----------|-------|-------|
| Embedded Shopify admin app | Stack B (Pod B) | Polaris Web Components, Admin GraphQL |
| Storefront on top of Shopify (Hydrogen) | Stack B (storefront mode) | Hydrogen + Oxygen, RR7 |
| Standalone ecom (any backend) | Stack C (Pod C) | Custom RR7 + Tailwind/shadcn |
| Boldteq SaaS dashboard | Stack A (Pod A) | Next.js 16 + Supabase |

NEVER mix: do not use Polaris on storefront, do not use Hydrogen for SaaS, do not use Next.js for embedded admin.

# Polaris ↔ Storefront Token Bridge

**Owner:** token
**Scope:** Stack B challenge — Shopify admin uses Polaris design system; storefront uses custom tokens. Brand must feel unified.

## The problem

Stack B apps embed in Shopify admin (Polaris-styled) AND ship a storefront the merchant's customers see (custom-styled). Two different design systems, same brand expectation.

Without a bridge: the admin uses Polaris navy + Inter; the storefront uses brand purple + Manrope. Merchants notice immediately.

## Mapping table (categories)

### Color
| Polaris token | Storefront token | Mapping rule |
|---------------|-----------------|--------------|
| `--p-color-bg-surface` | `--color-background` | Direct map (light/dark mode aware) |
| `--p-color-bg-fill-brand` | `--color-primary` | Brand color overrides Polaris default |
| `--p-color-text` | `--color-foreground` | Direct map |
| `--p-color-text-secondary` | `--color-muted-foreground` | Direct map |
| `--p-color-border` | `--color-border` | Direct map |
| `--p-color-bg-fill-critical` | `--color-destructive` | Direct map |

### Typography
| Polaris | Storefront | Mapping |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| `--p-text-heading-2xl` | `text-4xl` | Semantic equivalent |
| `--p-text-heading-xl` | `text-3xl` | |
| `--p-text-heading-lg` | `text-2xl` | |
| `--p-text-heading-md` | `text-xl` | |
| `--p-text-body-md` | `text-base` | |
| `--p-text-body-sm` | `text-sm` | |
| `--p-font-family-sans` | `font-sans` | Brand font preferred over Polaris default |

### Spacing
| Polaris | Storefront | Mapping |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| `--p-space-100` | `space-1` (4px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-200` | `space-2` (8px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-300` | `space-3` (12px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-400` | `space-4` (16px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-500` | `space-5` (20px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-600` | `space-6` (24px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-800` | `space-8` (32px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-1200` | `space-12` (48px) | Direct |

### Motion
| Polaris | Storefront | Mapping |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| `--p-motion-duration-100` | `--duration-instant` (100ms) | Direct |
| `--p-motion-duration-200` | `--duration-fast` (200ms) | Direct |
| `--p-motion-duration-300` | `--duration-base` (300ms) | Direct |
| `--p-motion-duration-500` | `--duration-slow` (500ms) | Direct |

## Gaps + decisions

### Polaris-only (no storefront equivalent)
- `--p-color-bg-fill-warning-secondary` → No storefront equivalent needed; warning UI lives in admin only
- Action: Accept divergence

### Storefront-only
- Hero gradient tokens (`--gradient-hero-from`, `--gradient-hero-to`) → No Polaris equivalent
- Action: Accept; gradients are storefront-specific

### Brand color override
- Polaris ships its own brand blue. Boldteq apps override with merchant's brand palette.
- Set `--p-color-bg-fill-brand` via Polaris's `AppProvider` theme prop or root CSS override.

## Implementation
- Storefront: ship `tokens.css` with `:root` + `.dark`
- Admin embed: in `App.tsx`, wrap in `<AppProvider i18n={...} theme={polarisTheme}>` where `polarisTheme` overrides brand color tokens
- Two CSS files load on different routes; no collision

## Verification
- Visual diff: open admin embed + storefront side-by-side; brand color should match
- Run contrast validation on both surfaces independently

# Figma Variable Sync

**Owner:** token
**Scope:** Bidirectional sync between codebase tokens and Figma variables via MCP.

## When to run
- Weekly Friday (token does sync as part of cadence)
- After token changes in code
- After designer requests sync via Vega

## Workflow

### Step 1: Pull Figma variables
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_variable_defs` on project Figma file
- Returns variable collections + modes (light/dark)
- Parse into JSON for comparison

### Step 2: Build comparison map
For each token in `tokens.css`:
- Find matching Figma variable by name (e.g., `--color-primary` ↔ `color/primary/default`)
- Compare values
- Flag drift: name mismatch, value drift, missing on either side

### Step 3: Decide direction
- **Code wins (default):** Most cases — code is source of truth. Push corrections to Figma via `create_design_system_rules`.
- **Figma wins (rare):** Only when Vega has approved a designer-led direction change. Update tokens.css.

### Step 4: Apply
- For code-wins: call `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__create_design_system_rules` with reconciliation list
- For figma-wins: edit `tokens.css`, regenerate Tailwind theme + shadcn JSON, run contrast validator

### Step 5: Emit reconciliation report
File: `memory/design/sync-reports/figma-sync-[YYYY-MM-DD].md`

Report structure:
1. Summary: drift count, decisions
2. Drift list (table: variable, codebase value, figma value, decision)
3. Action log
4. Next sync ETA

## Drift categories

### Name drift
- Token: `--color-primary`
- Figma: `color/Primary` or `Primary`
- Action: rename Figma variable to match codebase semantic naming

### Value drift
- Token: `222 47% 31%`
- Figma: `222 47% 35%` (designer adjusted in Figma)
- Action: investigate — was this designer-approved? If yes, update code. If accidental, push code value to Figma.

### Missing on Figma side
- Codebase has `--color-warning`; Figma collection doesn't
- Action: create Figma variable

### Missing on code side
- Figma has variable; codebase doesn't
- Action: triage — should code add it? If yes, add. If figma-only experiment, mark in Figma as `experimental`.

## Tools
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_variable_defs` — read variables
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__search_design_system` — search Figma library
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__create_design_system_rules` — push rules

## Sync target SLA
- Drift detected → reconciliation within 7 days
- Critical drift (brand color mismatch): same-day
PATH-END

CONTENT:
# JSX→.fig Pipeline

**Owner:** figma-synth
**Scope:** Convert shipped TSX components to Figma `.fig` deliverables.

## Pipeline stages

### Stage 1: TS AST parse
- Read TSX source: `components/[name].tsx`
- Use TypeScript compiler API or `ts-morph` to extract:
  - Component name
  - Prop types (interface or type alias)
  - Variants (often via `cva()` from class-variance-authority)
  - Default values
  - State variants (loading, disabled, error)
  - Responsive breakpoints (Tailwind classes parsed for `sm:`, `md:`, `lg:`)

### Stage 2: Render variant matrix
For each variant combination, determine the visual:
- Capture screenshots from a live storybook URL if project has Storybook running
- Or render mentally + use static screenshot for visual reference

### Stage 3: Token mapping
- Pull Token's variable map (`tokens.css` + Tailwind config)
- For each Tailwind class on the component, map to Figma variable
- Example: `bg-primary text-primary-foreground rounded-md` → Figma fill: `color/primary/default`, text color: `color/primary-foreground/default`, corner-radius: `radius/md`

### Stage 4: Build Figma component spec JSON
```json
{
  "name": "ProductCard",
  "type": "COMPONENT_SET",
  "variants": [
    {
      "props": {"variant": "default"},
      "fillId": "color/surface",
      "borderId": "color/border",
      "radiusId": "radius/lg"
    },
    {
      "props": {"variant": "sale"},
      "fillId": "color/surface",
      "badgeFillId": "color/destructive",
      "borderId": "color/border"
    }
  ],
  "propsPanel": [
    {"name": "title", "type": "TEXT"},
    {"name": "price", "type": "TEXT"},
    {"name": "image", "type": "INSTANCE_SWAP"},
    {"name": "variant", "type": "VARIANT", "options": ["default", "sale", "sold-out"]}
  ]
}
```

### Stage 5: Upload via Figma MCP
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__create_new_file` if no project Figma file exists
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__upload_assets` for any imagery referenced
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__use_figma` to write component to file

### Stage 6: Verify
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_design_context` on the new component
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_screenshot` for visual verification
- Compare against codebase render — flag drift

## Edge cases
- Generic types (e.g., `<Button<T>>`) — fall back to heuristic parse, flag for manual review
- Conditional rendering (`{loading && <Spinner/>}`) — represent as variant
- Composition (e.g., `<Card><CardHeader/></Card>`) — represent as instance + slots

## Output deliverable
- One Figma component per JSX component
- Variant matrix complete
- Token-mapped (no hardcoded hex)
- Asset uploads complete

## Coordination
- Token's variable map must be fresh (sync within 7 days)
- Vega owns the project Figma file admin rights
- Pod frontend notifies on component changes (so Figma-Synth can re-sync)
PATH-END

CONTENT:
# Code Connect Mapping Protocol

**Owner:** figma-synth
**Scope:** Bidirectional mapping between Figma components and codebase components.

## Why
Designers inspect a Figma frame → see actual codebase component import + props, not auto-generated placeholder code.

## Workflow

### Step 1: Identify mapping candidates
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_code_connect_suggestions` on project Figma file
- Returns components without mappings
- Cross-reference with codebase: `find components/ -name '*.tsx'`

### Step 2: Generate `.figma.tsx` mapping file

File location: `components/[name].figma.tsx` (alongside component source)

Template:
```tsx
import { figma } from "@figma/code-connect"
import { Button } from "@/components/button"

figma.connect(
  Button,
  "https://figma.com/file/[fileKey]/?node-id=[nodeId]",
  {
    props: {
      label: figma.string("Label"),
      variant: figma.enum("Variant", {
        "Primary": "primary",
        "Secondary": "secondary",
        "Ghost": "ghost",
        "Destructive": "destructive",
      }),
      size: figma.enum("Size", {
        "Small": "sm",
        "Medium": "md",
        "Large": "lg",
      }),
      disabled: figma.boolean("Disabled"),
      onClick: () => console.log("clicked"),
    },
    example: ({ label, variant, size, disabled }) => (
      <Button variant={variant} size={size} disabled={disabled}>
        {label}
      </Button>
    ),
  }
)
```

### Step 3: Register
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__add_code_connect_map` per component
- Then `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__send_code_connect_mappings` to publish to Figma

### Step 4: Verify
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_code_connect_map` → confirm mapping registered
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_context_for_code_connect` → confirm designer-facing snippet renders correctly

## Maintenance

### Daily sweep
- Run `get_code_connect_suggestions` to find newly added components without mappings
- For each, generate + register mapping

### Weekly audit
- For each registered mapping, check codebase component prop signature
- If changed: update `.figma.tsx`, re-register

### Breaking change protocol
- Component prop removed (e.g., `variant: 'success'` deleted)
- Update mapping immediately
- Notify Vega + designer working on that component
- If used in active Figma frames, suggest replacement variant

## Common patterns

### Boolean prop
```tsx
disabled: figma.boolean("Disabled"),
```

### Enum / variant
```tsx
variant: figma.enum("Variant", { "Primary": "primary", "Secondary": "secondary" }),
```

### Text content
```tsx
title: figma.string("Title"),
```

### Instance swap (for slots)
```tsx
icon: figma.instance("Icon"),
```

### Children
```tsx
children: figma.children(["Heading", "Description"]),
```

### Nested components
```tsx
header: figma.nestedProps("Header", {
  title: figma.string("Title"),
}),
```

## Anti-patterns
- Never delete a mapping without deprecation notice
- Never let mapping drift > 24h after component prop change
- Never hardcode example component without using the prop variables
PATH-END

# CRO Strategy Playbook

**Owner:** catalyst
**Scope:** Playbook for CRO strategy across ecom builds.

## Funnel stages + benchmarks

| Stage | Benchmark (median DTC) | Top quartile |
|-------|------------------------|--------------|
| Visitor → Cart | 5-8% | 12%+ |
| Cart → Checkout | 40-50% | 65%+ |
| Checkout → Purchase | 65-75% | 85%+ |
| First Purchase → Repeat | 25-35% | 50%+ |
| Subscriber retention (90d) | 55-65% | 80%+ |

## Lift mandate
40%+ relative improvement on baseline per surface tested.

## Test prioritization (ICE)
- **Impact (1-10):** Estimated revenue lift if winning
- **Confidence (1-10):** How sure are we this beats control? Decoder bank confidence boost.
- **Ease (1-10):** Implementation effort (10 = same-day, 1 = multi-week)
- **Score = I × C × E** (max 1000)
- Tests below 200 don't run

## Sequencing rules
- 1-2 tests live per project per week
- Don't run >3 tests on same surface simultaneously (cross-contamination)
- Holdout cohort for top tests (90/10 split, 8-week minimum)
- Statistical significance gate: 95% confidence + MDE met + 2-week run minimum

## Surface priority order (default)
1. PDP hero (highest leverage on first-touch)
2. Cart drawer mechanics
3. Checkout flow (steps, express, address)
4. Post-purchase upsell
5. Subscription toggle
6. Email signup discount
7. Listing filters
8. FAQ structure

## Per-niche adjustments
- Apparel: fit-finder UX often beats hero (size-uncertainty is #1 objection)
- Supplements: trust signals dominate (third-party testing > everything)
- Beauty: shade-finder + ingredient transparency
- Home: configurator UX, room-context photography
- Tech: spec-table positioning, comparison-with-competitors

## Playbook patterns

### Pattern 1: Above-fold trust trio
- Reviews stars + count
- Free shipping threshold
- 30-day return policy
Place above primary CTA. 8-15% lift on visitor→cart in skeptical niches.

### Pattern 2: Cart drawer free-shipping bar
- Threshold $50-80 (median)
- Progress bar with celebration on complete
- 12-18% AOV lift typical

### Pattern 3: Checkout express-first
- Shop Pay / Apple Pay / PayPal above the form on mobile
- Reduce mobile checkout abandonment 15-25%

### Pattern 4: Post-purchase one-click upsell
- 30-min eligibility window
- Single-click add (no re-payment)
- 8-15% AOV lift

### Pattern 5: Subscription default
- Default-select subscribe vs. one-time on PDP
- Caveat: only if churn-prevention strong
- 25-40% subscription rate lift

## Lessons captured
- Cross-project lessons append to `memory/patterns/good/cro-lessons-cross-project.md`
- Validated patterns promote to `cro-decoded-patterns.md`
- Failed patterns demote to `patterns/avoid/`
PATH-END

CONTENT:
# A/B Test Prioritization

**Owner:** catalyst
**Scope:** ICE-scored test roadmap + statistical significance gates.

## ICE Scoring

For every proposed test:

### Impact (1-10)
- 10: Above-fold PDP / hero (every visitor sees)
- 8: Cart drawer (every cart-creator)
- 7: Checkout step
- 6: Post-purchase upsell
- 5: Subscription toggle
- 4: FAQ rewrite
- 3: Listing filter UX
- 2: Footer CTAs
- 1: Account-page tweak

### Confidence (1-10)
- 10: Pattern observed in 8+ decoder brands and validated in past tests
- 8: Pattern in 5+ decoder brands
- 6: Pattern in 3+ decoder brands
- 4: Speculative; based on niche audit
- 2: Untested hypothesis

### Ease (1-10)
- 10: Same-day implementation
- 8: 2-3 day spec + ship
- 6: 1 week
- 4: 2 weeks
- 2: Multi-week effort

### Score = I × C × E (max 1000)

| Score | Decision |
|-------|----------|
| 600+ | Run this week |
| 300-600 | Queue next 2 weeks |
| 200-300 | Queue when bandwidth |
| <200 | Don't run |

## Statistical Significance Gates

Every test must hit ALL gates before declaring winner:

### Gate 1: Run length
- Minimum 14 days
- Captures full week cycle (weekday/weekend behavior)

### Gate 2: Sample size / MDE
- Compute MDE (Minimum Detectable Effect) for desired confidence
- Default: 95% confidence, 80% power
- For 5% baseline conversion + 10% MDE → ~22,000 visitors per variant
- Tools: Optimizely calculator, Evan Miller's calculator

### Gate 3: P-value < 0.05
- Two-sided test
- Bayesian alternative: 95% probability variant beats control

### Gate 4: No SRM (Sample Ratio Mismatch)
- Verify 50/50 split actually delivered ~50/50 traffic
- If skewed >5%, investigate instrumentation

### Gate 5: Effect size meaningful
- Lift must be ≥10% (don't ship 2% wins; not worth coordination cost)

## Test design rules

### Single-variable tests
- Default. Easy to attribute.

### Multi-variable tests
- Allowed for above-fold A/B/C variants from spark (3 variants of headline)
- Each variant must be a complete spec (not a/b/c on individual elements)

### Holdouts
- For top tests: 90/10 split
- Holdout cohort sees control for 8+ weeks even after winner declared
- Measures long-term retention impact (winner may lose at week 12)

### Sequential testing
- Allowed ONLY when test feeds next test (e.g., hero variant → bundle picker variant)
- Otherwise run parallel on independent surfaces

## Lift attribution

After test completion:
- Compute lift % vs control
- Verify gates 1-5
- Attribute to specialist (spark / ecom-cro / merch / sequence)
- Update `cro-decoded-patterns.md` with validated win
- Notify Echo + Yash via weekly CRO report

## Weekly cadence
- Monday: review prior week's results, declare winners/losers
- Tuesday: ship new variants (specialists)
- Wednesday: deploy to A/B framework
- Thursday-Sunday: monitor (Orbit dashboards)
- Friday afternoon: Decoder delta + roadmap update for next week
PATH-END

CONTENT:
# Hero Headline Formulas

**Owner:** spark
**Scope:** Niche-adapted headline formulas for ecom heroes.

## Universal rules
- ≤8 words
- Outcome-first
- Specific number when possible
- Active voice
- No banned words (leverage / synergy / innovative / seamless / robust / cutting-edge / next-gen / best-in-class)

## Per-niche formulas

### Apparel
- **Pain → Solution:** "Stop wearing scratchy wool. Start with merino."
- **Outcome + Material:** "Sleep-soft tees built to last."
- **Time-bound:** "Pack one, wear three days."
- **Anti-positioning:** "Not your grandfather's wool."

### Beauty
- **Outcome + Time:** "Glowing skin in 14 days."
- **Inclusive:** "60+ shades. One radical formula."
- **Ingredient-led:** "Hyaluronic acid, finally done right."
- **Result-vs-feature:** "Concealer that doesn't crease."

### Supplements
- **Specific benefit + Time:** "Energy in 5 minutes. No crash."
- **Quantified outcome:** "30 days to a stronger gut."
- **Trust-led:** "Third-party tested. Doctor formulated."
- **Anti-positioning:** "What your multivitamin missed."

### CPG (food/drink)
- **Sensory + Outcome:** "Cravings handled. Macros locked."
- **Indulgence-permission:** "Soda your gut will thank you for."
- **Number-led:** "20g protein. 4g sugar. Done."

### Home
- **Outcome + Time:** "Better sleep starts tonight."
- **Material-led:** "Organic cotton, made to outlast."
- **Anti-fast:** "Furniture that'll outlive your lease."

### Tech / connected
- **Outcome + Mechanism:** "Sleep deeper. Recover faster."
- **Spec-led benefit:** "Pod-tech sleep. Measurable proof."
- **Anti-tracker:** "More than a tracker. A sleep coach."

### Pet
- **Concern + Solution:** "Real food. Real ingredients. Tail-wagging proof."
- **Personalization:** "Your dog's perfect plate, delivered."

### Subscription / personal care
- **Convenience-led:** "Razors at your door. Half the price."
- **Anti-friction:** "Skincare without the guesswork."

## Subhead formulas
Pattern: **Pain acknowledgment + Solution mechanism + Proof hint**

≤25 words, 1-2 sentences.

Example:
- Headline: "Stop wearing scratchy wool. Start with merino."
- Subhead: "Hand-knit merino tees, 30-day comfort guarantee. Soft enough to sleep in. Worn by 200,000+."

## CTA formulas
≤4 words. Action verb + benefit.

| Niche | Low-friction | Standard | Commitment |
|-------|--------------|----------|------------|
| Apparel | "Try a tee" | "Shop merino" | "Add to bag" |
| Beauty | "See shades" | "Shop now" | "Get yours" |
| Supplements | "Start free" | "Try 30 days" | "Subscribe + save" |
| Subscription | "Join free" | "Get started" | "Subscribe" |

## Badge formulas
≤3 words. Announcement / category / status.

- "New collection"
- "Best seller"
- "Limited drop"
- "Just dropped"
- "Now subscription"
PATH-END

CONTENT:
# CTA Copy Variants

**Owner:** spark
**Scope:** Above-fold CTA copy generation.

## Universal rules
- ≤4 words
- Action verb first
- Benefit clear
- 3 sub-variants per primary CTA (low-friction / standard / commitment)

## Action verb library
- Start, Shop, Try, Get, Add, Build, Join, See, Browse, Pick, Choose, Find, Discover, Unlock, Save, Subscribe, Order, Reserve, Claim

## Avoid
- "Learn more" — too vague
- "Click here" — anti-pattern
- "Get started" — overused (use only when product-led signup)
- "Submit" — clinical
- "Sign up" — friction-prime

## Three-variant pattern (per dispatch)

### Low-friction
- Optimize for clicks (commitment can come later)
- Example: "Try free", "See shades", "Browse drops"

### Standard
- Optimize for ratio of click + intent
- Example: "Shop merino", "Get the kit", "Find your shade"

### Commitment
- Optimize for high-intent shoppers ready to buy
- Example: "Add to bag", "Subscribe + save 20%", "Order now"

## PDP-specific CTAs

### Add-to-Cart variants
- "Add to Bag" (apparel)
- "Add to Cart" (universal)
- "Get Yours" (commitment-led)
- "Buy Now" (urgency-prime, often paired with express checkout)

### Subscription toggle CTA
- "Subscribe + save 20%"
- "Lock in 15% off"
- "Set + forget"

### Variant trigger CTAs
- "Choose color"
- "Pick size"
- "Select bundle"

## Express checkout placement
Above the primary "Add to Cart" on mobile (decoder-validated):
- Shop Pay
- Apple Pay
- Google Pay
- PayPal

(Order matters: Shop Pay highest in Shopify ecosystem; Apple Pay highest cross-platform mobile)

## Multi-CTA hierarchy
Hero often has primary + secondary:
- Primary: commitment-prime ("Shop now")
- Secondary: low-friction ("See lookbook", "Watch video", "Read story")

Never 3+ CTAs above fold — dilutes attention.

## Microcopy adjacent to CTA
Trust-prime under CTA:
- "Free shipping over $50"
- "30-day returns, no questions"
- "No subscription required"

(spark provides this as a "secondary microcopy slot" tagged `merch-fill`; merch writes the actual text within voice rules)

CONTENT:
# Above-Fold Conversion Psychology

**Owner:** spark
**Scope:** Psychology behind above-fold copy decisions.

## The 5-second rule
Visitor decides whether to stay or bounce in 5 seconds. Above-fold copy has to:
1. Tell them what this is (recognition)
2. Tell them what they get (outcome)
3. Reassure them they're in the right place (proof)

## Cognitive load
- Headline: 1 idea
- Subhead: 1 expansion + 1 proof hint
- CTA: 1 next step
- Trust signal: 1 reassurance

If above-fold tries to convey >4 ideas, conversion drops.

## F-pattern + Z-pattern reading
- Desktop hero: F-pattern (top-left to right, then sweep down-left)
- Place headline top-left
- Place CTA below or top-right
- Place imagery on right side (visual weight)

- Mobile hero: Z-pattern is moot (single column)
- Stack: image → headline → subhead → CTA → trust signals
- Sticky CTA on long pages

## Specificity > generality
- "Save time" → 0% lift
- "Save 10 hours/week" → 8-15% lift (tested across decoder bank)
- "Better skin" → 0% lift
- "Glowing skin in 14 days" → 12-18% lift

## Outcome > feature
- Feature: "AI-powered scoring engine"
- Outcome: "Find your best candidates in seconds"
- Outcomes consistently outperform features 20-40% on first-touch

## Risk reversal
Place close to CTA:
- "30-day returns, no questions"
- "Free shipping over $50"
- "Cancel anytime"
- "No credit card required" (for SaaS — not ecom)

## Social proof types (descending efficacy)
1. Specific user testimonial w/ photo + name + outcome
2. Specific metric ("Used by 200,000+")
3. Logos of recognizable customers
4. Press mentions
5. Star rating + review count
6. Generic "Loved by thousands" (low value, used as default)

For first-time-visitor heroes: type 2 or 5 work best. Type 1 testimonials work better below fold.

## Skepticism in skeptical niches
- Supplements / health / wellness: trust signals dominate
- Place 3rd-party testing badge above CTA
- "Doctor formulated" or specific certifications
- Founder photo if founder is credentialed

## Above-fold trust trio (decoder-validated pattern)
Below CTA:
- Reviews stars + count
- Free shipping threshold
- 30-day returns

Drives 8-15% visitor→cart lift in apparel/beauty/CPG.

## Anti-patterns
- Hero video that auto-plays sound (instant bounce)
- Carousel hero with multiple slides (CTR drops on slides 2+; pick one)
- Long headline (>8 words eye-skips)
- Generic CTA ("Learn more")
- No specific number anywhere
- Trust signal placement below fold (too late)

## Niche intensity matrix
| Niche | Above-fold density | Notes |
|-------|--------------------|------|
| Apparel | High | Visual + headline + trust |
| Beauty | High | Visual-led, shade-finder prime |
| Supplements | Medium | Trust dominates over visual |
| Tech | Low | Spec-table + outcome, minimal visual |
| Home | Medium-High | Lifestyle photography + outcome |
| Subscription | Medium | Convenience-led, friction-removal |
PATH-END

CONTENT:
# Cart + Checkout Mechanics

**Owner:** ecom-cro
**Scope:** Below-fold cart + checkout mechanic specs.

## Cart drawer mechanics

### Trigger
- Auto-open on add-to-cart (default)
- Manual click on cart icon (always available)
- Never auto-open during active typing in another field

### State machine
- closed → opening (animation) → open → closing → closed
- During opening: backdrop fades in 200ms
- Open state: drawer slides in 320ms ease-out

### Components inside drawer
1. Header: "Your Cart (N items)" + close X
2. Free-shipping progress bar (if applicable)
3. Line items (scrollable)
4. Promo code field (collapsed by default)
5. Subtotal + tax + shipping breakdown
6. Express checkout buttons (above primary CTA on mobile)
7. Primary checkout CTA (sticky bottom mobile)
8. Trust badges row

### Line item interactions
- Quantity stepper: +/- buttons, debounced 200ms
- Remove: optimistic UI (immediate disappear), undo toast 5s
- Save-for-later (if logged in)
- Variant edit: opens bottom sheet

### Free-shipping progress bar
- Threshold: typically $50-80 (decoder-validated per niche)
- Progress %: (cart_subtotal / threshold) × 100
- Visual: filled bar with current % + remaining $X
- On completion: brief confetti + "Free shipping unlocked!" pulse
- Copy slot: merch fills "$X away from free shipping" / "Free shipping unlocked"

### Upsell row
- Show 1-3 recommended products
- Eligibility: not-already-in-cart, in-stock, related-by-tag
- Click → add without dismissing drawer
- Position: above subtotal (decoder pattern: 12% AOV lift)

## Checkout flow

### Step count
- Single-page checkout (default — best for mobile)
- Multi-step only for high-AOV / complex flows (e.g., custom configurations)

### Step order (single-page)
1. Email + contact (with returning-customer detection)
2. Shipping address (with autocomplete)
3. Shipping method
4. Payment (Shop Pay default + cards + BNPL)
5. Review

### Express checkout
- Position: above the form on mobile, above email on desktop
- Order: Shop Pay > Apple Pay > Google Pay > PayPal
- Mobile: 15-25% checkout abandonment reduction

### Address autocomplete
- Google Places API or Shopify-native
- Type 3 chars → suggestions appear
- Tap suggestion → auto-fills street, city, state, zip

### Field optimization
- Combine first + last name (single field) on mobile
- Postal code → numeric keyboard
- Phone → tel keyboard
- Card number → numeric + auto-detect type

### Order bump
- Pre-purchase one-click add (above payment)
- Single eligible product (high-margin, complementary)
- Click → add to cart, no re-confirm

### Returning customer
- Detect via email
- Pre-fill shipping address
- Show "Welcome back, {{firstName}}" microcopy slot

## Post-purchase upsell

### One-click eligibility
- Same payment method on file
- 30-min eligibility window
- Single eligible product
- Click → charge, no checkout re-flow

### Decline UX
- "No thanks" button → continue to thank-you
- Don't repeat upsell on next visit
- Track decline reason if survey opt-in

## Edge cases
- Sold-out item in cart: dim + "remove only" action
- Max-quantity hit: stepper disabled + tooltip slot for merch
- Subscription item: frequency display + "edit subscription" link slot
- Bundle ineligibility: hide upsell row, fall back to recommendations
- Shipping unavailable: error state with redirect to supported countries

## Coordination
- Elio: receives state machine + interaction map → produces visual spec
- Merch: receives copy slot list → fills text content
- Sequence: receives abandon trigger conditions
PATH-END

CONTENT:
# Upsell + Bundle Patterns

**Owner:** ecom-cro
**Scope:** Upsell, bundle, and order-bump mechanics.

## Bundle types

### Fixed bundle
- Pre-defined product set at discounted price
- Example: "Starter Kit (3 items, save 15%)"
- Pricing logic: bundle_price = sum(item_prices) × (1 - discount)
- UX: single PDP for the bundle, all items fixed

### Build-your-own bundle
- Customer picks N items from M-eligible pool, fixed total
- Example: "Build your 5-pack — any 5 sodas, $30"
- Pricing logic: total fixed; items unconstrained within pool
- UX: bundle picker on PDP or dedicated bundle page

### Tiered bundle
- Discount escalates with quantity
- "Buy 2, save 10%; buy 3+, save 15%; buy 5+, save 20%"
- Pricing logic: count_in_cart determines discount
- UX: progress display on PDP + cart

### Mix-and-match
- "Any 3 from collection X, save 15%"
- Pricing logic: tag-based eligibility, discount applied at cart level
- UX: callout on collection page + cart-level confirmation

## Order bump (pre-purchase)

### Position
- Above payment step in checkout (single-page)
- Above order review (multi-step)

### Eligibility logic
- Single product
- High-margin (don't bump cheap items)
- Complementary to cart (e.g., socks with shoes; not duplicate)
- In stock
- Not already in cart

### UX
- Single-click add (no re-confirm)
- Optimistic UI (line item appears immediately)
- "Added!" micro-confirmation
- Decline = ignore (no required interaction)

### Conversion math
- Typical bump conversion: 15-30% of viewers
- AOV lift: 5-10% across orders that see bump

## Post-purchase upsell

### Page placement
- After payment confirmation, before final thank-you
- One full page or modal

### One-click eligibility
- Same payment method on file
- 30-min eligibility window (Shopify limit; pattern varies by platform)
- Single product (don't show multiple — choice paralysis)
- Higher-AOV product than cart (upsell ladder)

### Decline UX
- "No thanks, take me to my order" → thank-you page
- Don't show same upsell on repeat visits

### Conversion math
- Typical post-purchase upsell conversion: 10-25%
- AOV lift: 8-15%

## Cart upsell row

### Position
- Inside cart drawer/page, between line items and subtotal
- Single row, 1-3 product recommendations

### Eligibility
- Not in cart
- Related-by-tag or "frequently bought together"
- In stock

### UX
- Compact card (image + title + price + "+" button)
- Click "+" → add to cart, no dismiss
- Updates free-shipping progress + subtotal in real-time

### Conversion math
- 8-15% of cart sessions add upsell row
- AOV lift: 4-8%

## Subscription upsell

### PDP toggle
- "One-time" vs "Subscribe & save 20%"
- Default: one-time (less commitment)
- Default-subscribe variant: 25-40% subscription rate lift, but only if churn-prevention strong

### Frequency picker
- 1mo / 2mo / 3mo / 6mo (per niche)
- Default: most popular for niche (decoder-validated)

### Skip / pause / cancel
- All self-serve (no email-required)
- Pause offer at cancel UX (Athletic Greens pattern: "skip a month" beats cancel 35% of attempts)

## Bundle math display
- Always show savings: "Bundle: $90 (save $15 vs. individual)"
- Use strikethrough for "individual price"
- Pre-calculate; never make the customer do math

## Anti-patterns
- Don't upsell items already in cart
- Don't bundle low-margin (kills profit per order)
- Don't show >3 cart-row upsells (decision fatigue)
- Don't auto-add bumps (ethics + chargebacks)
- Don't hide bundle savings — always display

## Decoder-validated patterns
- Athletic Greens: subscription default + pause-vs-cancel
- Magic Spoon: build-your-own 4-pack
- Liquid IV: tiered bundle (10/20/30 stick packs)
- Bombas: 4-pack discount on socks (commodity bundle)
- Olipop: variety pack as PDP
PATH-END

# Subscription Mechanics

**Owner:** ecom-cro
**Scope:** Subscription UX from PDP toggle through churn-prevention.

## PDP subscription toggle

### Default state
- One-time (default) — lower commitment, broader funnel
- Subscribe-default — only if niche has high churn-prevention or cart-friction is the bottleneck

### Display
- Two-option toggle: "One-time" / "Subscribe & save N%"
- Discount % visible in toggle (15-25% typical)
- Frequency picker appears when "Subscribe" selected
- Microcopy slot for merch: "Skip or cancel anytime"

### Frequency options
- Per-niche default:
  - Supplements: 1mo (most), 2mo, 3mo
  - CPG / food: 2 weeks, 1mo
  - Personal care: 1mo, 2mo, 3mo
  - Pet food: 2 weeks, 1mo (large bag)
- Default to most-popular frequency

## Subscription onboarding

### Welcome flow
- Email 1 (sequence): welcome + first-shipment ETA + skip/swap reminder
- In-app: first-shipment tracker, edit-subscription link
- Educational content: how to skip, how to swap, how to cancel

### First-shipment delight
- Branded packaging (Vega owns; sequence references)
- Insert card with "manage your subscription" QR
- First-month freebie or upgrade (decoder pattern: 8-12% retention lift)

## Mid-cycle engagement

### Pre-shipment notification
- 3 days before shipment: "Your next shipment is on its way"
- CTA: "Skip / swap / pause" (single-tap from email or in-app)

### Auto-pause-on-skip
- If customer skips 1+ time, offer pause: "Pause for 30/60/90 days?"
- Reduce churn vs full cancellation

## Cancellation UX (churn-prevention)

### Multi-step cancellation flow
1. "Why are you canceling?" → reason picker
2. Based on reason, offer save:
   - "Too much product" → reduce frequency
   - "Don't need right now" → pause (Athletic Greens pattern)
   - "Too expensive" → discount on next month
   - "Not the right fit" → swap to similar product
3. If still canceling: confirm with reduced-frequency offer
4. Final confirm: "Cancel subscription"

### Decoder-validated saves
- Athletic Greens: pause beats cancel 35% of attempts
- Hims: discount on next month beats cancel 20%
- Curology: swap-to-similar saves 15%

### Win-back trigger
- After cancellation: trigger win-back sequence (sequence owns)
- Day 30: "We miss you" + 20% off
- Day 60: "Last call — 25% off"
- Day 90: stop, respect unsubscribe

## Subscription account portal

### Required actions (self-serve)
- Skip next shipment
- Reschedule next shipment
- Swap product
- Change frequency
- Update payment method
- Update shipping address
- Pause (1/2/3 month)
- Cancel (with save flow)

### Anti-patterns
- Email-required to cancel — illegal in CA + EU per consumer law
- Hidden cancel link — same legal issue
- Unable to skip — drives cancellation instead

## Subscription analytics (Orbit owns; ecom-cro consumes)
- Active subscribers
- Churn rate (monthly + annualized)
- Average subscription lifetime (months)
- Skip rate per cycle
- Pause vs cancel ratio
- Win-back rate
PATH-END

CONTENT:
# PDP Body Structure

**Owner:** merch
**Scope:** Mandatory PDP body order + writing patterns.

## Mandatory order
1. Benefits-first paragraphs (2-3, ≤60 words each)
2. Benefit bullets (3-5)
3. Objection-handling section (3-5 objections)
4. Spec table

**NEVER lead with feature list.** This is the #1 anti-pattern.

## Section 1: Benefits paragraphs

### Pattern
- 2-3 short paragraphs
- Outcome-focused
- Specific numbers
- Customer language, not internal language
- Voice: confident, direct, no fluff

### Example (apparel — merino tee)
"Soft enough to sleep in, durable enough for daily wear. Our merino tee replaces 7 cotton tees in your rotation — and odor-resists for 3-day re-wear.

Sustainably sourced, machine-washable, made for life on the move. Pack one, wear three days, ship-it-back if it doesn't fit."

### Example (supplements — magnesium)
"Better sleep starts tonight. Magnesium glycinate, 350mg per dose — the form your body actually absorbs. No melatonin grogginess, no morning fog.

Third-party tested, manufactured in California, formulated by a clinical pharmacist. 30-day money-back guarantee."

## Section 2: Benefit bullets

### Pattern
- 3-5 bullets
- Each: outcome → mechanism
- Outcome bolded; mechanism plain

### Example
- **Sleep-soft fabric** — 18.5 micron merino, finer than human hair
- **3-day re-wear** — natural anti-odor, no synthetic finish
- **Machine-washable** — cold + tumble dry low, no special care
- **Carbon-neutral shipping** — verified offset on every order

### Anti-pattern
- "Made with merino wool" — that's a feature, not a benefit
- "Premium quality" — vague, no specificity

## Section 3: Objection-handling

### Pattern
- 3-5 objections (niche-typical)
- Each: 1 question + 1-2 sentence answer
- Address top objections inline (don't bury in FAQ alone)

### Niche-typical objections

#### Apparel
- "Will it itch?" / "How does it fit?" / "Care instructions?" / "Returns?"

#### Beauty
- "Will it work for my skin?" / "What if I'm allergic?" / "Is it cruelty-free?" / "Returns on opened products?"

#### Supplements
- "Is it safe?" / "How fast does it work?" / "Drug interactions?" / "Money-back guarantee?"

#### Tech / connected
- "Compatible with my devices?" / "Setup difficulty?" / "Data privacy?" / "Warranty?"

### Example (merino tee)
*Will it itch?*
This isn't your grandfather's wool. 18.5 micron sits below the itch threshold — softer than most cotton. If yours doesn't feel right, return it within 30 days, on us.

*How does it fit?*
True to size with a slight taper. Between sizes? Size up. Most reviewers say standard fit.

*Care instructions?*
Machine-wash cold, tumble dry low. No dry cleaning, no fabric softener — they coat the wool.

## Section 4: Spec table

### Pattern
- Utility format — short, factual
- No marketing voice
- Bullet pairs: label → value

### Example (merino tee)
- Material: 100% ZQ-certified merino wool, 18.5 micron
- Weight: 200 GSM (mid-weight)
- Fit: Standard, slight taper
- Care: Machine-wash cold, tumble dry low
- Origin: Knit in Portugal

### Anti-pattern
- "Crafted from luxurious 100% sustainably sourced premium-grade merino wool" — that's marketing voice in a spec table
- Just say: "100% merino wool, 18.5 micron"

## FAQ section (separate from objections)

### Pattern
- 5-10 questions, scan-friendly
- Beyond top objections — shipping, returns, account, subscription
- Sometimes structured as accordion

### Example questions
- Do you ship internationally?
- What's your return policy?
- How do I cancel a subscription?
- What if my item arrives damaged?
- Do you offer gift wrapping?

## Reading level + voice
- Grade ≤10 (target 8)
- Sentence length ≤20 words avg
- Paragraph length ≤3 sentences
- Quill voice scorecard 8/9
PATH-END

CONTENT:
# Objection Handling Frameworks

**Owner:** merch
**Scope:** Niche-typical objection patterns + frameworks for addressing.

## Universal framework
1. Acknowledge the concern (don't dismiss)
2. Provide the specific reassurance (number, policy, mechanism)
3. Risk reversal (return policy, guarantee, free trial)

## Per-niche objection libraries

### Apparel
| Objection | Answer pattern |
|-----------|----------------|
| Will it fit? | Size guide + true-to-size note + free returns |
| Will it shrink? | Care instructions + "no shrinkage" claim if true |
| Will it itch / scratch? | Material spec (micron count) + comfort guarantee |
| What if I don't like the color? | Free returns within 30 days |
| Returns process? | "Return free within 30 days, instant refund" |

### Beauty
| Objection | Answer |
|-----------|--------|
| Will it work for my skin type? | "Tested for [types]" + ingredient list |
| Allergic reactions? | Allergen-free claim + patch-test recommendation |
| Cruelty-free? | Certification (Leaping Bunny etc.) |
| Returns on opened products? | Policy ("opened, full refund within X days") |
| Right shade for me? | Shade-finder quiz / free shade match |

### Supplements
| Objection | Answer |
|-----------|--------|
| Is it safe? | Third-party testing + manufacturer info |
| Drug interactions? | "Consult doctor if on medications" |
| How fast does it work? | "Most users notice [effect] in [timeframe]" |
| Money-back guarantee? | "30-day full refund, no questions" |
| Subscription cancellation? | "Cancel anytime in your account, no fees" |

### CPG (food/drink)
| Objection | Answer |
|-----------|--------|
| Taste? | "Loved by N% of reviewers" + flavor profile |
| Allergens? | Full allergen list |
| Shelf life? | Months/years + freshness guarantee |
| Storage? | Room temp / refrigerated |

### Tech / connected
| Objection | Answer |
|-----------|--------|
| Setup difficulty? | "Set up in N minutes" + step count |
| Compatibility? | Device list + compatibility checker |
| Data privacy? | Privacy policy + on-device claim if applicable |
| Warranty? | Length + claim process |
| Returns? | 30/60/100-day policy |

### Pet
| Objection | Answer |
|-----------|--------|
| Picky pet? | "Money-back if pet refuses" |
| Right plan size? | Custom-plan calculator |
| Allergies? | Ingredient list + allergen-free options |
| Vet-recommended? | Vet endorsements + qualifications |

### Subscription / personal care
| Objection | Answer |
|-----------|--------|
| Commitment fear? | "Cancel anytime, no fees" |
| Right plan for me? | Quiz / consultation |
| Auto-renew? | "Reminder before renewal, easy skip" |
| Returns on unopened? | Policy |

## Risk reversal staples
- 30-day money-back guarantee
- Free shipping over $X
- Free returns
- Cancel anytime
- "If you don't love it, ship it back"
- First month free / risk-free trial

## Placement
- Top 3 objections inline in PDP body (per pdp-body-structure.md)
- Remaining objections in FAQ section
- Critical ones (returns, allergies) repeated in cart + checkout reassurance copy

## Voice
- Confident, not defensive
- Specific numbers (30 days, not "soon")
- Plain language
- Quill voice scorecard 8/9

## Anti-patterns
- "We're confident you'll love it" — generic
- "Most customers are happy" — vague
- "Email us if there's an issue" — high-friction
- Hiding cancellation behind email-required process — illegal in CA/EU
PATH-END

- "Order confirmed!" / "Thanks, {{firstName}}!" / "You're all set."

### Order details

- "We'll send a tracking number to {{email}} once it ships."

- "Top picks for you"

## Microcopy character limits
- Cart drawer header: ≤30 chars
- Free-shipping bar: ≤50 chars
- Trust badge label: ≤20 chars
- Primary CTA: ≤25 chars
- Error message: ≤80 chars
- Confirmation header: ≤40 chars

## Voice
- All microcopy passes quill voice scorecard 8/9
- No banned words
- Specific over generic ("$12 away" not "almost there")
- Active voice
- Confident, not apologetic

## Anti-patterns
- "Oops, something went wrong" — generic, no info
- "Please try again" — passive, no action
- "Add some products to your cart" — empty state should be more specific

- ALL CAPS labels (accessibility issue)

CONTENT:
# Cart Abandon Recovery Playbook

**Owner:** sequence
**Scope:** Recovery sequence specifics for cart abandon.

## Trigger conditions (set by ecom-cro, fired by sequence)
- Cart dismissed (drawer closed without checkout)
- 60 minutes elapsed
- Cart value > $30 (don't waste effort on low-value carts)
- Customer email captured (signed up or began checkout)
- Not purchased since trigger
- No prior abandon email in last 7 days

## 3-email cadence

### Email 1 — 1 hour
**Goal:** soft reminder, preserve margin
**No incentive.** Just a reminder.

| Element | Content |
|---------|---------|
| From | "{{brand}}" or "{{brandFounder}}" |
| Subject variants | "Forget something?" / "Your cart's still warm" / "Pick up where you left off" |
| Preview text | "Your cart's saved. Check out before stock changes." |
| Hero | Cart preview (item images + names) |
| Body | Soft reminder. No discount. |
| CTA | "Resume checkout" |
| Footer | Unsubscribe + brand info |

### Email 2 — 24 hours
**Goal:** incentive trigger (conditional)
**Discount IF cart value > $40, else free shipping IF cart > $80, else no discount.**

| Element | Content |
|---------|---------|
| Subject variants | "10% off — for the next 24h" / "{{firstName}}, here's a nudge" / "Save on what you almost bought" |
| Preview text | "10% off your cart. Code expires in 24h." |
| Hero | Discount banner + cart preview |
| Body | Discount code + 24h countdown + cart contents |
| CTA | "Apply discount + checkout" |

### Email 3 — 72 hours
**Goal:** final attempt
**Higher discount, alternatives shown, soft urgency.**

| Element | Content |
|---------|---------|
| Subject variants | "Last call: 15% off" / "Final reminder" / "Don't miss out" |
| Preview text | "15% off — final reminder." |
| Hero | 15% discount banner |
| Body | 15% code + cart preview + top 3 alternatives + "we'll release stock back" soft urgency |
| CTA | "Take 15% off" |

## Recovery rate targets
- Email 1: 2-4% recovery
- Email 2: 4-8% recovery
- Email 3: 1-3% recovery
- **Total sequence: 8-15% recovered carts**
- Top decoder benchmarks: 15-22%

## Discount escalation rules
- Never start with discount on email 1 (preserves margin + brand)
- Email 2: 10% if cart > $40, free ship if cart > $80, none if < $40
- Email 3: 15%, time-bound
- Don't go above 20% on cart-abandon (becomes habit-forming)

## Personalization
- {{firstName}} in subject (small lift)
- {{cartItems}} as preview content
- {{cartTotal}} for context
- Don't over-personalize (creepy zone)

## Send-time optimization
- Email 1: send any time (1h after trigger)
- Email 2: send Tue-Thu 10am local (best open rates)
- Email 3: send during business hours

## Decoder-validated patterns
- Bombas: 1h reminder no discount, 24h 15% off, 72h 20% off — recovers ~12% carts
- Chubbies: humorous voice, single email at 1h with $5 off — ~8% recovery
- Allbirds: 1h reminder, 24h "you have great taste" + free returns reminder — ~10% recovery

## Cross-sequence interaction
- If user added to cart again before sequence completes: pause sequence, restart trigger
- If user purchased: terminate sequence
- If unsubscribed: terminate
- If 7-day window elapsed without conversion: end sequence (don't re-trigger for 30d)

## Coordination
- Trigger logic: ecom-cro
- Email content: sequence
- Voice ratification: quill
- Brand kit: vega
- Email infra: postmark (when hired)
PATH-END

PATH: /Users/yashbaldha/.claude/skills/sequence/subscription-nurture-patterns.md
CONTENT:
# Subscription Nurture Patterns

**Owner:** sequence
**Scope:** Email sequences across subscription lifecycle.

## Subscription lifecycle stages

1. **Pre-renewal** — 3 days before next shipment
2. **Renewal** — shipment processed
3. **Post-shipment** — tracking + delight
4. **Mid-cycle** — between shipments, educational
5. **Cancel intent** — churn-prevention trigger
6. **Win-back** — post-cancellation

## Pre-renewal email (3 days before shipment)

### Goal
Notify + give skip/swap option (reduces churn 12-18%).

### Content
- Subject: "Your next shipment ships in 3 days"
- Hero: shipment preview (product + variant + frequency)
- Body: "We'll charge {{paymentMethod}} on {{date}}. Need to skip or swap? Update by {{cutoffDate}}."
- CTAs:
  - Primary: "Manage subscription"
  - Secondary inline links: "Skip this shipment" / "Swap product" / "Pause"

### Anti-pattern
- Don't bury skip/swap in account portal links — surface them in the email itself

## Post-renewal / shipped email

### Goal
Confirm + tracking + delight.

### Content
- Subject: "On its way! 📦"
- Body: tracking number + ETA
- Cross-sell: complementary products (without being pushy)
- CTA: "Track shipment"

## Mid-cycle engagement

### Goal
Keep brand top-of-mind between shipments. Reduce surprise-charge cancels.

### Cadence
- Subscription frequency = monthly: 1 mid-cycle email
- Frequency = bimonthly: 1-2 mid-cycle
- Frequency = quarterly: 2-3 mid-cycle

### Content patterns
- Educational: "5 ways to get more from your [product]"
- Community: "How customers are using [product]"
- Behind-the-scenes: brand story / new product preview
- User-generated content / reviews

### CTA
- Soft: "See more tips" / "Browse community posts"
- Avoid: aggressive cross-sell

## Churn-prevention sequence (cancel-intent trigger)

### Trigger
User clicks "Cancel" button in account portal.

### In-flow vs email
This typically happens in-app, but follow-up email reinforces the save offer.

### Email 1 (immediate post-cancel-attempt, if save offer accepted)
- Subject: "You're paused, not gone"
- Body: confirm pause duration + when subscription resumes + "any time, easy to update"

### Email 2 (immediate post-cancel-confirm, if save not accepted)
- Subject: "We're sorry to see you go"
- Body: "We've cancelled. Final shipment {{date}}. Re-subscribe anytime."
- Soft win-back hint: "If you change your mind, here's 20% off your first month back."

### Save-offer emails (sent if user clicks save)
- "Your subscription is paused for 30 days"
- "Frequency reduced to every 2 months"

## Win-back from cancel

### Trigger
30, 60, 90 days post-cancellation.

### Email 1 — Day 30
- Subject: "30 days off, on us"
- Body: re-activation incentive + soft "we updated [product]"
- CTA: "Re-subscribe"

### Email 2 — Day 60
- Subject: "Here's 20% off — come back"
- Body: discount + new arrivals
- CTA: "Use 20% off"

### Email 3 — Day 90
- Subject: "Last call"
- Body: 25% off + 7-day expiration
- CTA: "Use 25% off"

After 90: stop. Respect unsubscribe. Don't drift into re-engagement-spam zone.

## Subscription-specific copy notes

### Pause vs cancel framing
- Always offer pause as default save option
- Athletic Greens pattern: "Skip a month" before "Cancel"
- 35% of cancel-attempts convert to pause

### Frequency reduction
- "Most subscribers find every-2-months works better"
- Lower-frequency = lower-churn (counterintuitive)

### Discount-on-renewal
- Avoid — trains customers to threaten cancel for discounts
- Only deploy strategically (e.g., year-end retention push)

## Targets
- Pre-renewal email open: 45%+
- Mid-cycle open: 25%+
- Win-back recovery: 5-12%
- Cancel→pause rate: 30%+

## Coordination
- Trigger logic: ecom-cro
- Email content: sequence
- Subscription portal UX: ecom-cro
- Voice: quill

# Polaris ↔ Storefront Token Bridge

**Owner:** token
**Scope:** Stack B challenge — Shopify admin uses Polaris design system; storefront uses custom tokens. Brand must feel unified.

## The problem

Stack B apps embed in Shopify admin (Polaris-styled) AND ship a storefront the merchant's customers see (custom-styled). Two different design systems, same brand expectation.

Without a bridge: the admin uses Polaris navy + Inter; the storefront uses brand purple + Manrope. Merchants notice immediately.

## Mapping table (categories)

### Color
| Polaris token | Storefront token | Mapping rule |
|---------------|-----------------|--------------|
| `--p-color-bg-surface` | `--color-background` | Direct map (light/dark mode aware) |
| `--p-color-bg-fill-brand` | `--color-primary` | Brand color overrides Polaris default |
| `--p-color-text` | `--color-foreground` | Direct map |
| `--p-color-text-secondary` | `--color-muted-foreground` | Direct map |
| `--p-color-border` | `--color-border` | Direct map |
| `--p-color-bg-fill-critical` | `--color-destructive` | Direct map |

### Typography
| Polaris | Storefront | Mapping |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| `--p-text-heading-2xl` | `text-4xl` | Semantic equivalent |
| `--p-text-heading-xl` | `text-3xl` | |
| `--p-text-heading-lg` | `text-2xl` | |
| `--p-text-heading-md` | `text-xl` | |
| `--p-text-body-md` | `text-base` | |
| `--p-text-body-sm` | `text-sm` | |
| `--p-font-family-sans` | `font-sans` | Brand font preferred over Polaris default |

### Spacing
| Polaris | Storefront | Mapping |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| `--p-space-100` | `space-1` (4px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-200` | `space-2` (8px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-300` | `space-3` (12px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-400` | `space-4` (16px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-500` | `space-5` (20px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-600` | `space-6` (24px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-800` | `space-8` (32px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-1200` | `space-12` (48px) | Direct |

### Motion
| Polaris | Storefront | Mapping |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| `--p-motion-duration-100` | `--duration-instant` (100ms) | Direct |
| `--p-motion-duration-200` | `--duration-fast` (200ms) | Direct |
| `--p-motion-duration-300` | `--duration-base` (300ms) | Direct |
| `--p-motion-duration-500` | `--duration-slow` (500ms) | Direct |

## Gaps + decisions

### Polaris-only (no storefront equivalent)
- `--p-color-bg-fill-warning-secondary` → No storefront equivalent needed; warning UI lives in admin only
- Action: Accept divergence

### Storefront-only
- Hero gradient tokens (`--gradient-hero-from`, `--gradient-hero-to`) → No Polaris equivalent
- Action: Accept; gradients are storefront-specific

### Brand color override
- Polaris ships its own brand blue. Boldteq apps override with merchant's brand palette.
- Set `--p-color-bg-fill-brand` via Polaris's `AppProvider` theme prop or root CSS override.

## Implementation
- Storefront: ship `tokens.css` with `:root` + `.dark`
- Admin embed: in `App.tsx`, wrap in `<AppProvider i18n={...} theme={polarisTheme}>` where `polarisTheme` overrides brand color tokens
- Two CSS files load on different routes; no collision

## Verification
- Visual diff: open admin embed + storefront side-by-side; brand color should match
- Run contrast validation on both surfaces independently

# Figma Variable Sync

**Owner:** token
**Scope:** Bidirectional sync between codebase tokens and Figma variables via MCP.

## When to run
- Weekly Friday (token does sync as part of cadence)
- After token changes in code
- After designer requests sync via Vega

## Workflow

### Step 1: Pull Figma variables
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_variable_defs` on project Figma file
- Returns variable collections + modes (light/dark)
- Parse into JSON for comparison

### Step 2: Build comparison map
For each token in `tokens.css`:
- Find matching Figma variable by name (e.g., `--color-primary` ↔ `color/primary/default`)
- Compare values
- Flag drift: name mismatch, value drift, missing on either side

### Step 3: Decide direction
- **Code wins (default):** Most cases — code is source of truth. Push corrections to Figma via `create_design_system_rules`.
- **Figma wins (rare):** Only when Vega has approved a designer-led direction change. Update tokens.css.

### Step 4: Apply
- For code-wins: call `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__create_design_system_rules` with reconciliation list
- For figma-wins: edit `tokens.css`, regenerate Tailwind theme + shadcn JSON, run contrast validator

### Step 5: Emit reconciliation report
File: `memory/design/sync-reports/figma-sync-[YYYY-MM-DD].md`

Report structure:
1. Summary: drift count, decisions
2. Drift list (table: variable, codebase value, figma value, decision)
3. Action log
4. Next sync ETA

## Drift categories

### Name drift
- Token: `--color-primary`
- Figma: `color/Primary` or `Primary`
- Action: rename Figma variable to match codebase semantic naming

### Value drift
- Token: `222 47% 31%`
- Figma: `222 47% 35%` (designer adjusted in Figma)
- Action: investigate — was this designer-approved? If yes, update code. If accidental, push code value to Figma.

### Missing on Figma side
- Codebase has `--color-warning`; Figma collection doesn't
- Action: create Figma variable

### Missing on code side
- Figma has variable; codebase doesn't
- Action: triage — should code add it? If yes, add. If figma-only experiment, mark in Figma as `experimental`.

## Tools
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_variable_defs` — read variables
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__search_design_system` — search Figma library
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__create_design_system_rules` — push rules

## Sync target SLA
- Drift detected → reconciliation within 7 days
- Critical drift (brand color mismatch): same-day
PATH-END

# JSX→.fig Pipeline

**Owner:** figma-synth
**Scope:** Convert shipped TSX components to Figma `.fig` deliverables.

## Pipeline stages

### Stage 1: TS AST parse
- Read TSX source: `components/[name].tsx`
- Use TypeScript compiler API or `ts-morph` to extract:
  - Component name
  - Prop types (interface or type alias)
  - Variants (often via `cva()` from class-variance-authority)
  - Default values
  - State variants (loading, disabled, error)
  - Responsive breakpoints (Tailwind classes parsed for `sm:`, `md:`, `lg:`)

### Stage 2: Render variant matrix
For each variant combination, determine the visual:
- Capture screenshots from a live storybook URL if project has Storybook running
- Or render mentally + use static screenshot for visual reference

### Stage 3: Token mapping
- Pull Token's variable map (`tokens.css` + Tailwind config)
- For each Tailwind class on the component, map to Figma variable
- Example: `bg-primary text-primary-foreground rounded-md` → Figma fill: `color/primary/default`, text color: `color/primary-foreground/default`, corner-radius: `radius/md`

### Stage 4: Build Figma component spec JSON
```json
{
  "name": "ProductCard",
  "type": "COMPONENT_SET",
  "variants": [
    {
      "props": {"variant": "default"},
      "fillId": "color/surface",
      "borderId": "color/border",
      "radiusId": "radius/lg"
    },
    {
      "props": {"variant": "sale"},
      "fillId": "color/surface",
      "badgeFillId": "color/destructive",
      "borderId": "color/border"
    }
  ],
  "propsPanel": [
    {"name": "title", "type": "TEXT"},
    {"name": "price", "type": "TEXT"},
    {"name": "image", "type": "INSTANCE_SWAP"},
    {"name": "variant", "type": "VARIANT", "options": ["default", "sale", "sold-out"]}
  ]
}
```

### Stage 5: Upload via Figma MCP
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__create_new_file` if no project Figma file exists
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__upload_assets` for any imagery referenced
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__use_figma` to write component to file

### Stage 6: Verify
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_design_context` on the new component
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_screenshot` for visual verification
- Compare against codebase render — flag drift

## Edge cases
- Generic types (e.g., `<Button<T>>`) — fall back to heuristic parse, flag for manual review
- Conditional rendering (`{loading && <Spinner/>}`) — represent as variant
- Composition (e.g., `<Card><CardHeader/></Card>`) — represent as instance + slots

## Output deliverable
- One Figma component per JSX component
- Variant matrix complete
- Token-mapped (no hardcoded hex)
- Asset uploads complete

## Coordination
- Token's variable map must be fresh (sync within 7 days)
- Vega owns the project Figma file admin rights
- Pod frontend notifies on component changes (so Figma-Synth can re-sync)
PATH-END

CONTENT:
# Code Connect Mapping Protocol

**Owner:** figma-synth
**Scope:** Bidirectional mapping between Figma components and codebase components.

## Why
Designers inspect a Figma frame → see actual codebase component import + props, not auto-generated placeholder code.

## Workflow

### Step 1: Identify mapping candidates
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_code_connect_suggestions` on project Figma file
- Returns components without mappings
- Cross-reference with codebase: `find components/ -name '*.tsx'`

### Step 2: Generate `.figma.tsx` mapping file

File location: `components/[name].figma.tsx` (alongside component source)

Template:
```tsx
import { figma } from "@figma/code-connect"
import { Button } from "@/components/button"

figma.connect(
  Button,
  "https://figma.com/file/[fileKey]/?node-id=[nodeId]",
  {
    props: {
      label: figma.string("Label"),
      variant: figma.enum("Variant", {
        "Primary": "primary",
        "Secondary": "secondary",
        "Ghost": "ghost",
        "Destructive": "destructive",
      }),
      size: figma.enum("Size", {
        "Small": "sm",
        "Medium": "md",
        "Large": "lg",
      }),
      disabled: figma.boolean("Disabled"),
      onClick: () => console.log("clicked"),
    },
    example: ({ label, variant, size, disabled }) => (
      <Button variant={variant} size={size} disabled={disabled}>
        {label}
      </Button>
    ),
  }
)
```

### Step 3: Register
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__add_code_connect_map` per component
- Then `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__send_code_connect_mappings` to publish to Figma

### Step 4: Verify
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_code_connect_map` → confirm mapping registered
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_context_for_code_connect` → confirm designer-facing snippet renders correctly

## Maintenance

### Daily sweep
- Run `get_code_connect_suggestions` to find newly added components without mappings
- For each, generate + register mapping

### Weekly audit
- For each registered mapping, check codebase component prop signature
- If changed: update `.figma.tsx`, re-register

### Breaking change protocol
- Component prop removed (e.g., `variant: 'success'` deleted)
- Update mapping immediately
- Notify Vega + designer working on that component
- If used in active Figma frames, suggest replacement variant

## Common patterns

### Boolean prop
```tsx
disabled: figma.boolean("Disabled"),
```

### Enum / variant
```tsx
variant: figma.enum("Variant", { "Primary": "primary", "Secondary": "secondary" }),
```

### Text content
```tsx
title: figma.string("Title"),
```

### Instance swap (for slots)
```tsx
icon: figma.instance("Icon"),
```

### Children
```tsx
children: figma.children(["Heading", "Description"]),
```

### Nested components
```tsx
header: figma.nestedProps("Header", {
  title: figma.string("Title"),
}),
```

## Anti-patterns
- Never delete a mapping without deprecation notice
- Never let mapping drift > 24h after component prop change
- Never hardcode example component without using the prop variables
PATH-END

# CRO Strategy Playbook

**Owner:** catalyst
**Scope:** Playbook for CRO strategy across ecom builds.

## Funnel stages + benchmarks

| Stage | Benchmark (median DTC) | Top quartile |
|-------|------------------------|--------------|
| Visitor → Cart | 5-8% | 12%+ |
| Cart → Checkout | 40-50% | 65%+ |
| Checkout → Purchase | 65-75% | 85%+ |
| First Purchase → Repeat | 25-35% | 50%+ |
| Subscriber retention (90d) | 55-65% | 80%+ |

## Lift mandate
40%+ relative improvement on baseline per surface tested.

## Test prioritization (ICE)
- **Impact (1-10):** Estimated revenue lift if winning
- **Confidence (1-10):** How sure are we this beats control? Decoder bank confidence boost.
- **Ease (1-10):** Implementation effort (10 = same-day, 1 = multi-week)
- **Score = I × C × E** (max 1000)
- Tests below 200 don't run

## Sequencing rules
- 1-2 tests live per project per week
- Don't run >3 tests on same surface simultaneously (cross-contamination)
- Holdout cohort for top tests (90/10 split, 8-week minimum)
- Statistical significance gate: 95% confidence + MDE met + 2-week run minimum

## Surface priority order (default)
1. PDP hero (highest leverage on first-touch)
2. Cart drawer mechanics
3. Checkout flow (steps, express, address)
4. Post-purchase upsell
5. Subscription toggle
6. Email signup discount
7. Listing filters
8. FAQ structure

## Per-niche adjustments
- Apparel: fit-finder UX often beats hero (size-uncertainty is #1 objection)
- Supplements: trust signals dominate (third-party testing > everything)
- Beauty: shade-finder + ingredient transparency
- Home: configurator UX, room-context photography
- Tech: spec-table positioning, comparison-with-competitors

## Playbook patterns

### Pattern 1: Above-fold trust trio
- Reviews stars + count
- Free shipping threshold
- 30-day return policy
Place above primary CTA. 8-15% lift on visitor→cart in skeptical niches.

### Pattern 2: Cart drawer free-shipping bar
- Threshold $50-80 (median)
- Progress bar with celebration on complete
- 12-18% AOV lift typical

### Pattern 3: Checkout express-first
- Shop Pay / Apple Pay / PayPal above the form on mobile
- Reduce mobile checkout abandonment 15-25%

### Pattern 4: Post-purchase one-click upsell
- 30-min eligibility window
- Single-click add (no re-payment)
- 8-15% AOV lift

### Pattern 5: Subscription default
- Default-select subscribe vs. one-time on PDP
- Caveat: only if churn-prevention strong
- 25-40% subscription rate lift

## Lessons captured
- Cross-project lessons append to `memory/patterns/good/cro-lessons-cross-project.md`
- Validated patterns promote to `cro-decoded-patterns.md`
- Failed patterns demote to `patterns/avoid/`

# A/B Test Prioritization

**Owner:** catalyst
**Scope:** ICE-scored test roadmap + statistical significance gates.

## ICE Scoring

For every proposed test:

### Impact (1-10)
- 10: Above-fold PDP / hero (every visitor sees)
- 8: Cart drawer (every cart-creator)
- 7: Checkout step
- 6: Post-purchase upsell
- 5: Subscription toggle
- 4: FAQ rewrite
- 3: Listing filter UX
- 2: Footer CTAs
- 1: Account-page tweak

### Confidence (1-10)
- 10: Pattern observed in 8+ decoder brands and validated in past tests
- 8: Pattern in 5+ decoder brands
- 6: Pattern in 3+ decoder brands
- 4: Speculative; based on niche audit
- 2: Untested hypothesis

### Ease (1-10)
- 10: Same-day implementation
- 8: 2-3 day spec + ship
- 6: 1 week
- 4: 2 weeks
- 2: Multi-week effort

### Score = I × C × E (max 1000)

| Score | Decision |
|-------|----------|
| 600+ | Run this week |
| 300-600 | Queue next 2 weeks |
| 200-300 | Queue when bandwidth |
| <200 | Don't run |

## Statistical Significance Gates

Every test must hit ALL gates before declaring winner:

### Gate 1: Run length
- Minimum 14 days
- Captures full week cycle (weekday/weekend behavior)

### Gate 2: Sample size / MDE
- Compute MDE (Minimum Detectable Effect) for desired confidence
- Default: 95% confidence, 80% power
- For 5% baseline conversion + 10% MDE → ~22,000 visitors per variant
- Tools: Optimizely calculator, Evan Miller's calculator

### Gate 3: P-value < 0.05
- Two-sided test
- Bayesian alternative: 95% probability variant beats control

### Gate 4: No SRM (Sample Ratio Mismatch)
- Verify 50/50 split actually delivered ~50/50 traffic
- If skewed >5%, investigate instrumentation

### Gate 5: Effect size meaningful
- Lift must be ≥10% (don't ship 2% wins; not worth coordination cost)

## Test design rules

### Single-variable tests
- Default. Easy to attribute.

### Multi-variable tests
- Allowed for above-fold A/B/C variants from spark (3 variants of headline)
- Each variant must be a complete spec (not a/b/c on individual elements)

### Holdouts
- For top tests: 90/10 split
- Holdout cohort sees control for 8+ weeks even after winner declared
- Measures long-term retention impact (winner may lose at week 12)

### Sequential testing
- Allowed ONLY when test feeds next test (e.g., hero variant → bundle picker variant)
- Otherwise run parallel on independent surfaces

## Lift attribution

After test completion:
- Compute lift % vs control
- Verify gates 1-5
- Attribute to specialist (spark / ecom-cro / merch / sequence)
- Update `cro-decoded-patterns.md` with validated win
- Notify Echo + Yash via weekly CRO report

## Weekly cadence
- Monday: review prior week's results, declare winners/losers
- Tuesday: ship new variants (specialists)
- Wednesday: deploy to A/B framework
- Thursday-Sunday: monitor (Orbit dashboards)
- Friday afternoon: Decoder delta + roadmap update for next week
PATH-END

# Hero Headline Formulas

**Owner:** spark
**Scope:** Niche-adapted headline formulas for ecom heroes.

## Universal rules
- ≤8 words
- Outcome-first
- Specific number when possible
- Active voice
- No banned words (leverage / synergy / innovative / seamless / robust / cutting-edge / next-gen / best-in-class)

## Per-niche formulas

### Apparel
- **Pain → Solution:** "Stop wearing scratchy wool. Start with merino."
- **Outcome + Material:** "Sleep-soft tees built to last."
- **Time-bound:** "Pack one, wear three days."
- **Anti-positioning:** "Not your grandfather's wool."

### Beauty
- **Outcome + Time:** "Glowing skin in 14 days."
- **Inclusive:** "60+ shades. One radical formula."
- **Ingredient-led:** "Hyaluronic acid, finally done right."
- **Result-vs-feature:** "Concealer that doesn't crease."

### Supplements
- **Specific benefit + Time:** "Energy in 5 minutes. No crash."
- **Quantified outcome:** "30 days to a stronger gut."
- **Trust-led:** "Third-party tested. Doctor formulated."
- **Anti-positioning:** "What your multivitamin missed."

### CPG (food/drink)
- **Sensory + Outcome:** "Cravings handled. Macros locked."
- **Indulgence-permission:** "Soda your gut will thank you for."
- **Number-led:** "20g protein. 4g sugar. Done."

### Home
- **Outcome + Time:** "Better sleep starts tonight."
- **Material-led:** "Organic cotton, made to outlast."
- **Anti-fast:** "Furniture that'll outlive your lease."

### Tech / connected
- **Outcome + Mechanism:** "Sleep deeper. Recover faster."
- **Spec-led benefit:** "Pod-tech sleep. Measurable proof."
- **Anti-tracker:** "More than a tracker. A sleep coach."

### Pet
- **Concern + Solution:** "Real food. Real ingredients. Tail-wagging proof."
- **Personalization:** "Your dog's perfect plate, delivered."

### Subscription / personal care
- **Convenience-led:** "Razors at your door. Half the price."
- **Anti-friction:** "Skincare without the guesswork."

## Subhead formulas
Pattern: **Pain acknowledgment + Solution mechanism + Proof hint**

≤25 words, 1-2 sentences.

Example:
- Headline: "Stop wearing scratchy wool. Start with merino."
- Subhead: "Hand-knit merino tees, 30-day comfort guarantee. Soft enough to sleep in. Worn by 200,000+."

## CTA formulas
≤4 words. Action verb + benefit.

| Niche | Low-friction | Standard | Commitment |
|-------|--------------|----------|------------|
| Apparel | "Try a tee" | "Shop merino" | "Add to bag" |
| Beauty | "See shades" | "Shop now" | "Get yours" |
| Supplements | "Start free" | "Try 30 days" | "Subscribe + save" |
| Subscription | "Join free" | "Get started" | "Subscribe" |

## Badge formulas
≤3 words. Announcement / category / status.

- "New collection"
- "Best seller"
- "Limited drop"
- "Just dropped"
- "Now subscription"
PATH-END

# CTA Copy Variants

**Owner:** spark
**Scope:** Above-fold CTA copy generation.

## Universal rules
- ≤4 words
- Action verb first
- Benefit clear
- 3 sub-variants per primary CTA (low-friction / standard / commitment)

## Action verb library
- Start, Shop, Try, Get, Add, Build, Join, See, Browse, Pick, Choose, Find, Discover, Unlock, Save, Subscribe, Order, Reserve, Claim

## Avoid
- "Learn more" — too vague
- "Click here" — anti-pattern
- "Get started" — overused (use only when product-led signup)
- "Submit" — clinical
- "Sign up" — friction-prime

## Three-variant pattern (per dispatch)

### Low-friction
- Optimize for clicks (commitment can come later)
- Example: "Try free", "See shades", "Browse drops"

### Standard
- Optimize for ratio of click + intent
- Example: "Shop merino", "Get the kit", "Find your shade"

### Commitment
- Optimize for high-intent shoppers ready to buy
- Example: "Add to bag", "Subscribe + save 20%", "Order now"

## PDP-specific CTAs

### Add-to-Cart variants
- "Add to Bag" (apparel)
- "Add to Cart" (universal)
- "Get Yours" (commitment-led)
- "Buy Now" (urgency-prime, often paired with express checkout)

### Subscription toggle CTA
- "Subscribe + save 20%"
- "Lock in 15% off"
- "Set + forget"

### Variant trigger CTAs
- "Choose color"
- "Pick size"
- "Select bundle"

## Express checkout placement
Above the primary "Add to Cart" on mobile (decoder-validated):
- Shop Pay
- Apple Pay
- Google Pay
- PayPal

(Order matters: Shop Pay highest in Shopify ecosystem; Apple Pay highest cross-platform mobile)

## Multi-CTA hierarchy
Hero often has primary + secondary:
- Primary: commitment-prime ("Shop now")
- Secondary: low-friction ("See lookbook", "Watch video", "Read story")

Never 3+ CTAs above fold — dilutes attention.

Trust-prime under CTA:
